Subject: Astra-Lite evaluation + onboarding questions

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We ran a lightweight benchmark overnight (attached) and are excited about Astra-Lite (3B) for a customer-facing assistant proof-of-concept. Before we move forward we have a few operational asks:

- Can Redwood support a temporary routing exemption so requests from our us-west customers go to a pinned low-latency variant while broader compatibility tests run?
- What intake artifacts do you need from us (tokenizer tests, sample prompts, PSF)?
- We have SOC2 evidence requests and a security questionnaire — will you accept our PDF or do you need specific logs/audit records?

I've attached the bench CSV and the security questionnaire. Procurement is cc'd for contract timing.

Looking for a short checklist and an estimated time-to-onboard.

—Sarah

Subject: Re: Astra-Lite evaluation + onboarding questions

Thanks for the ping — quick technical read:

1) Tokenizer/compat: Astra-Lite uses a byte-level tokenizer variant; we should ask Nebula to provide ~1000 representative prompts and a short tokenization report (counts, OOV examples). That will tell us whether we need a tokenizer shim or to serve the model with a hosted tokenizer.

2) Variant pinning/routing exemption: feasible as a temporary policy. We can create an ephemeral alias (astra-lite/nebula-usw-pin) bound to a quantized variant optimized for latency. Constraints:
   - Requires a reserved GPU slot for expected QPS (we need their target RPS).
   - KV cache priming recommended to avoid early cold-start latency.

3) Quantization + kernels: the model appears friendly to int8/llm.int8 pathways, but we'll run a short verifier pass (fast-lint) to ensure no operator gaps. Expect 48–72 hours for the compatibility run if they provide sample artifacts today.

I can own the verification. If Nebula wants the routing exemption for a week while we run compatibility tests, we can approve a provisional alias but only after procurement signs an SLA addendum covering capacity and fallback behavior.

Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-06-24T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Astra-Lite evaluation + onboarding questions

Appreciate the summary. Product-side asks and proposed timeline:

- Intake checklist (high priority): sample prompt set (1k), tokenizer report, expected SLOs (p95 latency target), expected traffic profile (RPS and concurrency), and business-critical safety examples.
- QA window: once sample artifacts are in, product + QA will need 5 business days for regressions and output quality checks. If Karthik's compatibility run is 48–72 hours, we can overlap the tasks and be ready to toggle full routing in ~7 business days.
- Temporary routing exemption: I support a provisional alias with constraints: 1) only for a named subset of customers, 2) auto-revert policy after 7 days unless we manually approve extension, 3) telemetry hooks (latency/error/quality) must be exposed to Nebula and our account team.

Action items:
- Alex: send a clear onboarding checklist and propose a kickoff time.
- Karthik: run the verifier once we get the sample prompts and share any kernel/operator mismatches.
- I'll prepare a short customer-facing onboarding plan and the SLA addendum template for procurement.

Marissa
Director of Product — Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah — thanks for the bench and questionnaire. Short plan and next steps: 

1) Intake checklist (what we need from you): 1k sample prompts, tokenizer report (counts/OOV), expected p95 latency target and RPS, and confirmation of which customers should be routed to the provisional alias.
2) Technical verification: Karthik will run a 48–72 hour compatibility/quantization verification once we have the artifacts; he flagged that int8 paths look promising.
3) Routing exemption: We can provisionally create an alias pinned to a latency-optimized variant in us-west under a 7-day auto-revert policy. This requires procurement sign-off on the SLA addendum (Marissa will send).
4) Security evidence: we're happy to take your PDF questionnaire; our security team will review and return any missing items within 3 business days.

Can you share the sample prompts and confirm target RPS? Also propose a 30-min kickoff tomorrow at 10:30am PT if that works.

Best,
